# Preface {.unnumbered}

## Vivax Serology Partnership 

A global partnership between academia, biotechnology industry research and development, non-governmental organisations, policy and implementation stakeholders to address a major gap in the diagnosis of *Plasmodium vivax* infections and accelerate towards elimination. 

For more information see the [VISPA website](https://vispa.online/). 

## Purpose of This Book

This book aims to provide a step-by-step tutorial on how to analyse serology data, with a particular focus on our *Plasmodium vivax* serology test and treat (PvSeroTAT) strategy. It also covers pathogen-agnostic workflows for users applying `{SeroTrackR}` to other serology data.

## SeroTrackR 

`{SeroTrackR}` is a tool for serology data analysis and visualisation, and for the application of the machine learning algorithms implemented in the `{PvSeroApp}`. The R package is intended to give users more flexibility in assessing serology data and manipulate data visualisations to the user's interest. 

Function reference documentation and vignettes are available on the [pkgdown site](https://dionnecargy.github.io/SeroTrackR/).

You can install the R package from CRAN: 

```{r}
#| eval: false
install.packages("SeroTrackR")
library(SeroTrackR)
```

Alternatively you can install the development version from GitHub using the `{pak}` R package: 

```{r}
#| eval: false
if(!require(pak)){
  install.packages("pak") # If not already installed
} 
pak::pak("dionnecargy/SeroTrackR")
library(SeroTrackR)
```

Note that the GitHub (development) version bundles the trained classification model file locally, whereas the CRAN version downloads it at runtime, so the CRAN version requires an internet connection the first time functions such as `classifyResults()` are called.
